# Nehemiah Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and our other enemies learned that I had finished rebuilding the wall — with no gaps left, though I had not yet hung the gates —

**2** Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message: "Come, let's meet in one of the villages on the plain of Ono." They were plotting to harm me.

**3** I sent back this reply: "I'm engaged in an important project and cannot come down. Why should the work grind to a halt just so I can meet with you?"

**4** They sent the same invitation four times, and four times I gave the same answer.

**5** The fifth time, Sanballat sent his aide with an open, unsealed letter — deliberately meant for everyone to read.

**6** It said: "Word is spreading among the surrounding nations — and Geshem confirms it — that you and the Jews are plotting a revolt. That's why you're building the wall. And according to reports, you intend to make yourself king.

**7** You've even appointed prophets to announce in Jerusalem: 'Judah has a king!' The Persian king will certainly hear these rumors. So you'd better come and talk this over with us."

**8** I sent back my answer: "None of what you're saying is happening. You're making it all up."

**9** They were all trying to intimidate us, calculating that we would lose our nerve and abandon the work. I prayed, "Now, God, give me strength."

**10** One day I visited Shemaiah son of Delaiah, grandson of Mehetabel, who was confined to his house. He said, "Let's meet in God's temple — inside the sanctuary itself — and bar the doors, because men are coming tonight to kill you."

**11** I replied, "Should someone in my position run and hide? And how could a man like me — not a priest — enter the sanctuary and survive? I will not go."

**12** Then I realized that God had not sent this man. He had fabricated this "prophecy" against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him off.

**13** Their scheme was to make me afraid, to get me to violate God's law by entering the sanctuary, and then to use my sin against me to destroy my reputation.

**14** I prayed, "Remember what Tobiah and Sanballat have done, O my God. Remember also the prophetess Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to terrorize me."

**15** The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul — just fifty-two days after we began.

**16** When our enemies heard the news, and all the surrounding nations saw what had happened, they were demoralized and deeply shaken. They recognized that this work could only have been accomplished with God's help.

**17** During this whole period, the nobles of Judah were in constant correspondence with Tobiah, sending and receiving letters.

**18** Many in Judah had ties of loyalty to him, since he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.

**19** These nobles kept praising Tobiah's virtues to me while reporting everything I said back to him. Meanwhile, Tobiah kept sending letters designed to frighten me.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **Escalating tactics** — The enemies deploy increasingly sophisticated strategies: invitation (vv. 2-4), public smear campaign (vv. 5-7), and finally a hired false prophet attempting spiritual manipulation (vv. 10-13). Each attack targets a different vulnerability — physical safety, reputation, and spiritual integrity.
2. **"I am doing a great work"** — Nehemiah's famous refusal (v. 3) is a model of focused faithfulness. He recognizes that the greatest threat to God's work is not opposition but distraction.
3. **Fifty-two days** — The wall's completion in less than two months is the narrative's climax. Even Israel's enemies recognize the divine fingerprint (v. 16), turning military defeat into theological testimony.

*— PNEUMA*
